hypothesis: Half of the first forward after a SnapStart restore (0.68 s against 0.24 s warm, P3) is memset inside llama_kv_cache::clear and llama_memory_recurrent::clear: the per-request llama_memory_clear(mem, true) zeroes every K/V and recurrent buffer, and after a restore that is the first touch of those pages. At llama.cpp f74e2fa6a the zeroing is not needed for correct results: the KQ mask gives every empty attention cell -INFINITY, and the recurrent cache zeroes one state row in the graph (build_rs, rs_z) and copies it into every cell a sequence starts in. Resetting only the cache metadata (llama_memory_clear(mem, false)) should make the restored first request about 0.3 s faster and warm requests about 2% faster, with bit-identical answers.

In every (round, CPU part) cell every e12 row is faster than every dor row. Restore first request total (Restore Duration + Duration) on 0xd40: {restore_first_request_total_0xd40_dor:.3f} -> {restore_first_request_total_0xd40_e12:.3f} s ({restore_first_request_total_0xd40_pct:+.1f}%, CI [{restore_first_request_total_0xd40_lo:+.3f}, {restore_first_request_total_0xd40_hi:+.3f}]). Lambda's own Restore Duration, which runs before any function code, is unchanged ({restore_report_restore_duration_0xd40_d:+.3f} s, CI [{restore_report_restore_duration_0xd40_lo:+.3f}, {restore_report_restore_duration_0xd40_hi:+.3f}]), as it should be. The hypothesis (about 0.3 s, half of 0.68 s) holds. Warm: on 0xd40 steady-state inference p50 {warm_steady_state_inference_0xd40_dor:.3f} -> {warm_steady_state_inference_0xd40_e12:.3f} s ({warm_steady_state_inference_0xd40_pct:+.2f}%, CI [{warm_steady_state_inference_0xd40_lo:+.3f}, {warm_steady_state_inference_0xd40_hi:+.3f}]); paired by request and round the median ratio is {warm_ratio_0xd40:.4f} (CI {warm_ratio_0xd40_ci}, {warm_ratio_0xd40_cells} cells), so the hypothesised ~2% warm gain is not established. The warm effect splits by request: requests no longer than one the environment already ran change by {reach_within_seen_0xd40_pct:+.1f}% (0xd40, median over requests), and requests that reach further into the caches than any earlier one in their environment change by {reach_new_max_0xd40_pct:+.1f}%. The likely reason is that e12 defers the first touch of never-written cache pages from the clear into that request's forward; this is an inference (Lambda allows no fault counting) and the split is confounded with the fixed warm request order. Cold: the first request total is unchanged ({cold_first_request_total_0xd40_d:+.3f} s, CI [{cold_first_request_total_0xd40_lo:+.3f}, {cold_first_request_total_0xd40_hi:+.3f}]); the 25 s S3 download still binds. Correctness: {errors} errors (no client:ReadTimeoutError) and {mismatches} class mismatches in {invocations} invocations; {ref_identical} of {ref_compared} answers P1's reference covers are bit-identical to it, and {agree_identical} of {agree_compared} e12 answers equal the dor answers for the same request and CPU part (P1's five requests plus four stress requests: a 16-question fork over a 2.8k-token state, then short requests on the cells it left). Offline on arm64 (not Lambda): P1's own shim, the dormant switch and DEC_CLEAR_DATA=0 return identical answers and identical hidden-state bytes for every request in 6 shuffled orders x 3 repeats ({offline_rows} rows, pass={offline_pass}), with no dependence on what ran before. The shim reported its mode from inside every environment (dor 1, e12 0). Max memory used moves by {cold_report_max_memory_mb_0xd40_d:+.1f} MB cold and {restore_report_max_memory_mb_0xd40_d:+.1f} MB restored (p50, 0xd40). Scope: this applies to Lambda (SnapStart) only, not to SageMaker-hosted models (operator scope note, 2026-10-21). The saving is the first touch of SnapStart-restored cache memory, and the warm effect alone is not established; SageMaker was not measured here. Recommendation: adopt DEC_CLEAR_DATA=0 for Lambda SnapStart deployments; a ladder rung should re-measure it with E10 (smaller n_ctx shrinks the same buffers) and consider touching the caches once before the snapshot to remove the deferred first-touch cost on long requests.
